analysis: Examined units: docs/reference/configuration.md head lines 312-597. The only changed line is 594, a documentation note that a bf16 GPT-OSS checkpoint keeps bf16 activations, so MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE does not apply to it. The note is informational and has no security effect. The surrounding SSD prefix-cache table (lines 498-529) is unchanged. It covers the TTL cap of 1800 s, the KEK, ephemeral fallback and the kill switch, and remains consistent with T-041. EngineV2Bridge.swift lines 132-136 change only a doc comment: kvBytesPerToken is now described as priced from observed native per-layer K/V types via EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken, instead of a GPT-OSS fp32-delta description. No code changed in this file. The capacity/reservation behavior (availability, T-029/T-041 staging budget) depends on slotKVBytesPerToken in EngineV2SlotFactory, which is not supplied in this batch. Integration should verify that heartbeats and process-wide reservations still cannot overstate capacity. In particular, an underpriced K/V rate could overcommit memory; that would be an availability concern, not confidentiality. The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moves from 0351444e to f2eb29b8. The submodule contents are not supplied, which is a coverage limit. This in-process inference library is part of TB-007 and handles decrypted prompts (A-001). Its changes could affect native KV dtype or sizing, prefix-cache codecs (T-041) and residual memory (T-028). These cannot be assessed here, and deeper review of the submodule diff is recommended. No concrete regression was identified in the supplied evidence.
